title: Check a reading's references to earlier jobs against the repo
summary: Add a check in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, run when a reading is built, that confirms each earlier job id, path, role, or symbol the reading relies on exists in the snapshot (landed, with a path found). Otherwise the reading must list it as a deliverable to create, or put it in out_of_scope. Audience: the planner, critic and verifier, who now find missing dependencies late. Jobs 20261026-042558-5p65, 20261026-064950-38jx and 20261026-065228-02zf are the referenced earlier attempts; their candidate work is not touched here.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust in crates/athena-core.
A new test fails without the check; fmt, clippy and test pass.
Fixed at reading acceptance, where unverified references are first admitted.
Criteria run cargo test on the refusal and acceptance cases.
Enforced by a check in code, not prose.
One check in one file plus notes.
The outcome is that missing dependencies are caught at reading, shown by tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs: build_reading (line 542) is the entry point; check_prior_result_and_scope (2391) and check_code_survey (2999) run after resolution, and the new check goes beside them. The new check adds no record or data file, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are unaffected. The property is measured directly by calling the new check on a Reading with fixture snapshot paths.

Root cause: nothing verifies that artifacts the reading says already exist (paths, files, symbols named in the request or notes) are present in the snapshot; a job id is taken to mean its work landed.

Scope of the check: paths under crates/, docs/ and similar that the reading's text names as existing and does not list as create deliverables or out_of_scope. A named item that is not found must be a create deliverable or in out_of_scope, else the reading is refused.

Past jobs 20261026-042558-5p65, 20261026-064950-38jx and 20261026-065228-02zf are not retried here; their candidate files (code_health.rs and others) are neither kept nor created by this change and are excluded in out_of_scope.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml) need no change: the check is code, with no new configuration field.
Refusal rate: the check refuses more readings; the higher rate is intended; expected 8% of newly refused readings.

acceptance_criteria.text: The CHANGELOG.md entry and the change description name the root cause: readings take a named earlier job's deliverable as existing without checking the snapshot, and the fix sits in the reading-acceptance check in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs.

A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs gives a reading that says an existing path or role from a queued earlier job is already there. The check refuses it, and the same reading is accepted when the item is a create deliverable, in out_of_scope, or present in the snapshot. Run: cargo test -p athena-core reading. The test fails without the change.
The test uses at least two distinct missing dependencies (a path and a symbol or role), so the class is covered and not one job's case. Run: cargo test -p athena-core reading.
The change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 8% of newly refused readings.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test all pass.

out_of_scope: Retrying the code-health, context-engineer or other jobs 20261026-042558-5p65, 20261026-064950-38jx, 20261026-065228-02zf; their candidate files (crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs, steward.rs, status.rs, gh.rs, display.rs, run.rs, introspect.rs, jev.rs, records.rs, briefs.rs) are dropped, not kept
departures: Hard reading-rule change touching a large file; slightly higher cost and lower pass odds than reference.
urgent_reason: It cuts failed planning stops and rejected attempts, where the critic is the first to find a dependency that never landed.
hard_reason: Adds a rule at reading acceptance that can refuse readings, so a mistake would wrongly hold work.
